references.text: The same pattern is repeated: The children of Israel cry out to the Lord, and he raises up a deliverer (Ehud) to rescue them.
The children of Israel cry out to the Lord under Jabin's oppression, following the same pattern as with Othniel.
Israel cries out to the Lord under the oppression of the Midianites, and the Lord sends a deliverer (Gideon).
Israel cries out to the Lord and confesses their sin, and the Lord delivers them repeatedly.
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, is first mentioned here as the conqueror of Kiriath-Sefer.
Othniel son of Kenaz is mentioned as Caleb's brother who conquered Kiriath-Sefer.
Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite is mentioned as being faithful to the Lord.
The children of Israel groan under slavery in Egypt and cry out to God, who hears their cry and raises up Moses as a deliverer.
Israel's cry has reached God, and he sends Moses as a deliverer—the same pattern as with Othniel.
Samuel reminds the people how they cried out to the Lord, and he sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel as deliverers.
God gave them deliverers who rescued them from the hand of their enemies when they cried out to him.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
